title: About the station
text: Larkspur Research Station is a fictional coastal field station invented for this example. It sits on Brenna Point and is staffed from March to November.

title: Solar power
text: The station's main power comes from a 48 kW solar array on the north ridge. A 30 kWh battery bank stores surplus solar energy for use at night.

title: Backup generator
text: The backup generator runs on biodiesel. It is test-run every Tuesday at 09:00 for fifteen minutes, and the duty engineer records the fuel level afterwards.

title: Server room
text: The server room is kept at 21 °C. If the server room temperature rises above 27 °C, the duty engineer must shut down the analysis cluster.

title: Analysis cluster
text: The analysis cluster has six nodes with one GPU each. Jobs expected to run longer than four hours must be booked on the cluster calendar.

title: Data backups
text: Field data is backed up every night at 02:30 to the archive server named Heron. A weekly copy is shipped to the mainland office on Sundays.

title: Network
text: The satellite link provides 40 Mbit/s of download capacity. Video calls are restricted to the library between 18:00 and 20:00.

title: Boats
text: The station has two boats: Gannet for inshore sampling and Petrel for offshore work. No boat may launch when the wind exceeds 25 knots.

title: Diving rules
text: Every dive needs a buddy and a surface supervisor. The maximum depth for station dives is 18 metres.

title: Weather station
text: The automatic weather station logs wind speed, rainfall and air pressure every 10 minutes. Its data feed is called WX-Brenna.

title: Sample storage
text: Water samples are kept in the cold room at 4 °C. Frozen tissue samples are stored in the minus-80 freezer labelled F2.

title: Chemical safety
text: Formalin may only be handled in fume hood 3. Waste formalin is collected in the yellow drums beside the loading dock.

title: Medical care
text: The station manager is the first-aid officer. The nearest hospital is in Kestrel Harbour, 45 minutes away by boat.

title: Emergencies
text: When the fire alarm sounds, everyone gathers at the muster point by the flagpole beside the boathouse. Radio channel 16 is monitored at all times.

title: Accommodation
text: Visiting researchers stay in the Tern bunkhouse, which has twelve beds. Quiet hours are from 22:00 to 07:00.

title: Meals
text: Meals are served in the mess hall at 07:30, 12:30 and 18:30. Dietary requirements must reach the cook one week before arrival.

title: Vehicles
text: The station's only road vehicle is an electric utility truck. It is charged from the solar array and must be plugged in overnight.

title: Library
text: The library holds the station logbooks back to 1998 and a reference collection of field guides. Logbooks may not leave the library.

title: Kelp survey
text: The kelp survey has run every August since 2004 along transect K7, south of the jetty.

title: Seabird counts
text: Puffin burrows on Skerry Island are counted each June. Landing on Skerry Island requires a permit from the regional wildlife office.

title: Tide gauge
text: The tide gauge at the end of the jetty records the water level every 6 minutes and sends its readings to the archive server once an hour.

title: Waste and recycling
text: Recycling is collected on Thursdays. Food waste goes to the compost bays behind the vegetable garden.

title: Drinking water
text: Drinking water comes from a rainwater cistern and is treated with ultraviolet light. The cistern holds 60,000 litres.

title: Wet lab booking
text: The wet lab is booked through the front office. Bookings open two weeks ahead and are limited to three days per project.

title: Induction
text: New staff complete the boat safety course on their first Monday and the radio course in their first week.

title: Energy reporting
text: Each month the station manager reports biodiesel use and solar yield to the trustees, together with the battery bank's state of health.
